criteria.check: Read metrics.py (only module doing arithmetic), graph.py draft() which hands the model met.as_table() + policy rules only, and finalise() whose stamp numbers come from GuardResult counts. grep for arithmetic outside metrics.py found none in the memo path.

Read every Metric constructor in compute(). M6 evidence is sliced [:50], M9 [:200], M15 [:200]; on the cafe synthetic statement M9 lists 200 of 362 operating lines and M6 50 of 291 overdrawn lines, so the figure cannot be traced to all its lines. M10 lists only loan ids though computed from operating cash flow too. test_every_metric_cites_evidence only checks ids exist, not completeness.

Read graph.py draft(): user prompt is account name, period dates, met.as_table(metrics) and policy rules. as_table emits id/name/display/method only; no transaction fields reach the model. No test inspects the prompt FakeLLM receives, so this is proven by reading only.

Graph flow (route_after_guard, MAX_REDRAFTS=2, interrupt payload guard_grounded) read and covered by test_hallucinating_model_is_caught_and_redrafted. But guard.check skips the missing-citation check for any metric value that is an integer <= 31 without £/%: memo 'The account was overdrawn on 25 days.' with M6=25 returns grounded=True, missing_citations=[]. Count/day metrics (M1, M6, M7, M13) drive policy rules R1, R3, R4, R5 and can be quoted uncited.

test_graph_stops_for_review_then_finalises proves no final_memo before resume. But reviewer identity is not required: ReviewDecision.reviewer defaults to 'analyst', review() accepts a bare bool resume, and the interactive CLI path builds the decision without a reviewer. Probe: graph.invoke(Command(resume=True)) finalised with 'Reviewed by analyst: APPROVED.'

Read categorise.py: ordered RULES, first match wins, unmatched credit -> OTHER, unmatched debit -> SUPPLIER. Satisfied by reading. The OTHER branch is never exercised by any test because synth never emits an unmatched credit (grep OTHER tests/ -> no hits).

Read policy/uk_sme_default.yaml and policy.py evaluate(): thresholds, ops, on_fail and refer bands all come from YAML; no thresholds in prompts or code. Refer bands (refer_below/refer_above) and on_fail mapping have no direct unit test; test_policy_separates_profiles only checks overall outcome on cafe.

Read synth.py ARCHETYPES/CUSTOMER_NAMES (fictional, commented as such), examples/cafe_stretched.csv (387 lines, descriptions match synth templates e.g. 'CARD ACQUIRER SETTLEMENT', 'SO RENT PARKGATE ESTATES'), evals/results/ is gitignored. No real-looking personal or employer data found.

Probed ingest.load_csv with seven malformed CSVs. Inconsistent running balances (T2 balance 999 after +5 on 10) ACCEPTED; duplicate ids (two rows 'T1') ACCEPTED; missing column raises bare KeyError('amount'), not a clear error. Bad date / non-numeric amount / header-only do raise. No tests/test_ingest.py exists.

Read .github/workflows/ci.yml: pip install, ruff, pytest, evals with --llm fake; get_llm defaults to FakeLLM; AnthropicLLM/OpenAILLM import SDKs lazily. Ran pytest locally: 38 passed in 0.71s with no key set.
tests/test_metrics.py::test_metrics_match_truth asserts M2, M5, M6, M7, M8, M11, M12 against synth Truth within 0.01 across all 9 archetype x profile cases; ran and passed.

Probed guard.check. NUMBER regex's trailing lookahead (?![A-Za-z\d]) makes the engine backtrack to a shorter match instead of rejecting: '1.5x' is read as '1' (plain int, allowed) so an invented '1.5x' DSCR passes grounded=True with zero findings; '£22.4k' is read as '£22' so the k-suffix variant at guard.py:31 is unreachable. Also '[M10]' yields a stray '0' that inflates numbers_checked and grounding_rate.

findings.claim: NUMBER regex backtracks on a trailing letter instead of rejecting, so a number written with a unit suffix ('1.5x', '£22.4k', '264.3k') is matched as its leading integer. An invented ratio '1.5x' passes the guard as a plain prose integer; '£22.4k' is flagged with the wrong text '£22', and the 'k' variant at line 31 can never match.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from cma.guard import check, NUMBER; from cma.models import Metric; m=[Metric(id='M10',name='c',value=1.42,unit='ratio',method='x'), Metric(id='M3',name='avg',value=22400.0,unit='GBP',method='x')]; print([x.group(0) for x in NUMBER.finditer('1.5x')]); g=check('Cover should be 1.5x.', m); print(g.grounded, g.unmatched); g=check('Average monthly revenue was £22.4k [M3].', m); print(g.grounded, [f.number_text for f in g.unmatched])"  -> ['1'] / True [] / False ['£22']

findings.claim: The missing-citation check is skipped whenever the metric value is an integer <= 31 without £ or %. R4 requires every metric value to carry its [Mn] tag in the same sentence; P2's small-integer exemption applies to unmatched numbers, not to citations. Count/day metrics M1, M6, M7, M13 (which drive policy rules R1, R3, R4, R5) can therefore be quoted with no citation and the memo is still 'grounded'.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from cma.guard import check; from cma.models import Metric; m=[Metric(id='M6',name='Days overdrawn',value=25,unit='days',method='x')]; g=check('The account was overdrawn on 25 days, which is poor.', m); print(g.grounded, g.missing_citations)"  -> True []

findings.claim: M15 (top counterparty share) keys payers by description words [2:5], which hard-codes synth's 'FPS CREDIT <name> INV####' layout. A two-word payer gets its invoice number folded into the key, so each invoice counts as a separate customer and concentration is understated. On the trades synthetic statement this yields 37 'counterparties' for 8 customers. Policy rule R7 (threshold 60%) reads M15, so a concentrated book can pass. M15 has no ground-truth test (not in P1's list, not in test_metrics).
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from datetime import date; from cma.models import Statement, Transaction; from cma import categorise, metrics; rows=[('T1','FPS CREDIT T WHITTAKER INV1001',1000),('T2','FPS CREDIT T WHITTAKER INV1002',1000),('T3','FPS CREDIT T WHITTAKER INV1003',1000),('T4','FPS CREDIT ELMS DENTAL PRACTICE INV2001',1000)]; b=0; t=[]; exec('for i,(tid,d,a) in enumerate(rows):\n b+=a; t.append(Transaction(id=tid,date=date(2026,1,1+i),description=d,amount=a,balance=b))'); s=categorise.categorise(Statement(account_name='x',transactions=t)); print({m.id:m.value for m in metrics.compute(s)}['M15'])"  -> 25.0 (expected 75.0)

findings.claim: Evidence lists are truncated: M6 evidence[:50] (line 89), M9 evidence[:200] (line 97), M15 evidence[:200] (line 112). On every cafe statement M9 cites 200 of 362 operating lines and M6 50 of 291 overdrawn lines, so the figure cannot be traced to the statement lines it was computed from. test_every_metric_cites_evidence checks only that cited ids exist, never that the list is complete. Separately M10's evidence lists only loan ids though its value also depends on every operating line (line 100).

findings.claim: Reviewer identity is optional, not required. ReviewDecision.reviewer defaults to the placeholder 'analyst'; graph.review() (graph.py:129-130) accepts a bare bool resume and fills in the default; the interactive CLI path (cli.py:70) builds the decision dict with no reviewer. The final memo is then stamped 'Reviewed by analyst' as though an identity had been recorded. No test asserts a reviewer must be supplied.

Inconsistent running balances are accepted (M5/M6 then computed from bad balances); duplicate transaction ids are accepted (by_id() silently drops one, breaking evidence lookup); a missing column surfaces as a bare KeyError('amount') rather than a clear message. There is no tests/test_ingest.py.

findings.claim: The lookbehind (?<![A-Za-z]) does not exclude a preceding digit, so the trailing digit of every citation tag is counted as a number: '[M10]' yields '0', '[M15]' yields '5'. numbers_checked and therefore grounding_rate (the headline eval metric) are inflated; a FakeLLM memo with 15 cited figures reports 21 numbers checked.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from cma.guard import NUMBER, check; from cma.models import Metric; print([m.group(0) for m in NUMBER.finditer('[M10] [M15]')]); print(check('Cover is 1.42 [M10]. Returned DDs: 1 [M7].', [Metric(id='M10',name='c',value=1.42,unit='ratio',method='x'), Metric(id='M7',name='r',value=1,unit='count',method='x')]).numbers_checked)"  -> ['0', '5'] / 3

findings.claim: When there is no debt service, M10 is set to the sentinel 99.0 and displayed as '99.00' in the metrics table; the model is then invited to write 'debt service cover of 99.00 [M10]' and policy rule R2 passes on a fabricated ratio. A magic number stands in for 'not applicable'.
findings.repro: Read src/cma/metrics.py:50 (dscr = inf when debt_service == 0) and :98 (value=... else 99.0). Any statement with no LOAN_REPAYMENT lines reproduces it.

findings.claim: The load -> categorise -> compute pipeline is assembled by hand in three places: mcp_server.compute_metrics (line 35), mcp_server.check_policy (line 42) and the graph's load/categorise/metrics nodes (graph.py:74-81). There is no single function that owns 'statement path to metrics', so a change such as adding validation or a cache has three call sites to update and the MCP tools can drift from what the graph computes.

Test coverage gaps against the requirements: no test for ingest (R9); no direct test for the categoriser's unmatched-credit -> OTHER branch (R6; synth never emits an unmatched credit, so the 9-case truth test never reaches categorise.py:33-35); no unit test for policy refer bands, on_fail mapping or a custom policy path (R7); no test that the draft prompt excludes transactions (R3); no truth test for M3, M4, M9, M10, M13, M14, M15 (M15 defect above went unnoticed); nothing for cli.py or mcp_server.py.
